title: Long-Term Effects of Environmental Lead on Erythropoietin Production in Young Adults: A Follow-Up Study of a Prospective Cohort in Kosovo.
ehr_evidence: BPb measurements from childhood were already available from the parent cohort study, measured every six months from birth through age 12 years; those measurements were conducted in the same laboratory using the same method.
summary: Follow-up study of a prospective birth cohort in Kosovo examining the long-term effects of environmental lead exposure on erythropoietin production in young adults.
key_findings: Positive association between concurrent BPb and serum EPO levels after adjusting for hemoglobin (β = 0.19; 95% CI 0.06, 0.31).
Significant positive associations found between cumulative BPb (AUC birth-age 2, ages 2-4, ages 4-7) and EPO, though associations diminished with age.
No significant relationship between log BPb and log serum EPO in the unadjusted model (β = 0.05; 95% CI −0.09, 0.20).
Mean serum EPO concentration was significantly higher in the exposed town of Mitrovica (10.99 mIU/ml) compared to Prishtina (8.49 mIU/ml; P < 0.04).
data_source_type: prospective cohort with laboratory assays and questionnaires
population: 101 young adults (mean age 24.9 years) from a birth cohort in Mitrovica and Pristina, Kosovo
limitations: small follow-up sample size (20% of original cohort)
12.5-year gap between childhood measurements and follow-up
lack of bone marrow biopsy and liver function tests
limited generalizability to lower exposure populations or other regions
data_availability_statement: All pertinent data are in our study files and can be made available upon request.
